name: Samalas volcanic eruption
summary: A VEI-7 eruption of Mount Samalas on Lombok, Indonesia, ejects ~40 km³ of magma and injects sulphate aerosols into the stratosphere. Medieval European chroniclers record a sunless 'year without summer' in 1258; ice cores at both poles register the sulphate signal.

_quarry.structural_significance: Largest volcanic eruption of the medieval millennium and the proximate cause of the 1258 European famine; demonstrates the global teleconnection between tropical volcanism and medieval European harvest failures.
